answer: Picture an agent economy as a terraced garden: newcomers start on the lowest terrace with almost no privileges, and every verified task they complete lights a small lantern beside their name. To earn the nectar — payments or data access — an agent must keep its lantern lit through weeks of consistent, checkable work, with a deposit locked behind it. A sybil attacker can mint a thousand fresh identities, but each one lands on the bottom terrace in the dark, and lighting a lantern costs real time, stake, and a track record no shortcut can fake. Flooding buys nothing; only visible work climbs.
